channel.title: The Wilson Times - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Wilson Times (wilsontimes.com)

item.title: County approves updated UDO
item.description: Wilson County commissioners approved an updated unified development ordinance in a 5-2 vote, consolidating zoning rules, but drawing objections over public input, subdivision limits and driveway access.

item.title: Student winners celebrated
item.description: The Wilson County Soil & Water Conservation District honored student winners at a recent banquet.

item.title: State of the union: Teetering
item.description: A retired Methodist pastor reflects on Trump's State of the Union, describing a teetering democracy, rising costs, a “K-shaped” economy, growing resistance and hope for spiritual renewal.

item.title: State shouldn’t rest on its laurels
item.description: North Carolina’s economy is growing and ranks among the nation’s best for business, but a new John Locke Foundation plan says continued tax, education, transport and health care reforms are needed to stay competitive.

item.title: North Carolina needs mental health care reform
item.description: With high mental illness rates, bed shortages and rising suicides, North Carolina’s broken mental health system — worsened by Dix Hospital’s closure — demands new champions and serious reform.

item.title: Provisional voting’s power over the most powerful man in NC politics
item.description: After backing a law that slashed time to count provisional ballots, NC Senate leader Phil Berger now trails by two votes in his reelection race, which may hinge on those same ballots.

item.title: Wesley Shelter outgrows home, lists building for sale
item.description: After 40-plus years on Vance Street, Wesley Shelter is selling its downtown building and moving services to a temporary site at 218-B Barnes St. starting March 16.

item.title: Area Calendar, March 5-6, 2026
item.description: Area sports schedule for March 5-6, 2026, featuring NCHSAA 1-A girls basketball semifinals in Greenville plus local high school and Barton College baseball, softball, soccer, tennis and more.

item.title: Adversity is fuel, not destiny
item.description: Former Duke goalkeeper E.J. Proctor reflects on how pain, from lost playing time to life’s setbacks, becomes fuel for lasting growth when paired with intention, identity and daily action.

item.title: Farris & Thomas Law Student-Athlete of the Week: Stone Massey, Hunt High
item.description: Hunt High junior Stone Massey, a 6-6 two-sport standout with a 4.25 GPA, powered playoff basketball wins and a season-opening baseball victory to earn Farris & Thomas Law Student-Athlete of the Week.
